- **Slide 2 (hook)** connects to the paper's opening move of using everyday multi-role experience (student, child, sibling, etc.) to foreshadow the George example in "Ontology and Assignment"
- **Slides 3–5 (the problem / George)** directly recount the paper's central illustration (pp. 4–5)
  - George as teacher-and-son mirrors Benzon's own worked example of contradictory inheritance (authoritative teacher vs. submissive son)
  - The "contradiction" framing matches Benzon's claim that a single paradigmatic hierarchy would make George "both submissive and authoritative"
- **Slide 6 (two trees)** condenses Benzon's core theoretical apparatus
  - Paradigmatic tree ↔ Figure 2 (VAR/IST "isa" hierarchy, properties inherited downward)
  - Assignment tree ↔ Figure 1 (ASN hierarchy, properties inherited upward: object→plant→animal→human→social person)
- **Slide 7 (fix for George)** reproduces Benzon's resolution in Figure 4 — roles are assigned (ASN) to the human being, not inherited, so identity and role stay separate
- **Slide 8 (food example)** is a faithful compression of the paper's "food" case (pp. 5–6, Figure 5)
  - Apple/beef as functional-paradigm members despite no shared substantive ancestor
  - "Substantive vs. functional paradigms" terminology taken directly from the paper
- **Slides 9–10 (caterpillar vs. expulsion)** map onto Benzon's paradigmatic-vs-ontological transition distinction (pp. 6–7)
  - Caterpillar→butterfly ↔ the paper's own "Caterfly" example (Figure 6): same identity, changed form = paradigmatic transition
  - Expulsion as composition/decomposition of a role-layer generalizes Benzon's own examples (exile, christening, marriage) of ontological transition as loss/gain of assigned structure
- **Slides 11–12 (CIMWorld)** summarize the paper's extended engineering case study (pp. 8–14)
  - Object→Assembly→Mechanism→Engine→Computer hierarchy matches Figure 7/8's assignment chain
  - Machining-as-paradigmatic vs. assembly-as-ontological (imaginary→real connectivity) echoes the paper's "instance migration" and "satisfaction of connectivity" discussion (Figures 9–11)
  - PhysWorld/InfoWorld split reproduces Figure 12 and the completeness/causal-coherence requirements
- **Slide 13 (water/H₂O)** is the student's substitution for Benzon's own salt/sodium-chloride opening example, used to illustrate the paper's "multiple ontologies" section (novice vs. expert ontologies, pp. 15–16)
- **Slides 14–17 (evaluation and take)** extend beyond the paper itself
  - Slide 14's strengths list credits the paper's real contributions (multi-role identity separation, cross-domain generality)
  - Slides 15–17 pivot to the student's own argument (LLMs as pattern-matchers without explicit ontological structure) — not sourced from Benzon (writing in 1985, pre-LLM) but framed as a modern test of whether his 1985 problem has since been solved or merely sidestepped
